title: A privileged enumerator matches programs by path pattern and then executes them
index_line: T-0059 · EXEC · root-run service discovery regex-matches binaries and runs each with `-v` · c/any-inventory-agent · corroborated
invariant_violated: An inventory/discovery agent is assumed to be read-only: it looks at the machine and reports. But identifying a program means asking it for its version, and asking means executing. A privileged agent that decides what counts as a program by matching a path pattern hands the unprivileged user both halves of the exploit — they choose the path and the contents.

mechanism.does: an unprivileged local user places an executable at a path that matches the agent's service pattern
the privileged agent (running as root, or via a root-owned tunnel to the hypervisor) walks the filesystem and applies its pattern
the path matches, so the agent treats the file as a service binary and selects the version command for it
the agent executes the attacker's file with that command, in its own privileged context
the file's code runs as root before any version output is parsed

source.env.value: the local filesystem namespace — the input is where the attacker can write, not a network request

fs.path.join.value: the search-path resolution that decides which files match the pattern

guard.none.value: no ownership check, no allow-list of trusted directories, no signature on what it executes

sink.exec.noshell.value: the agent's execution of a discovered binary to obtain its version

preconditions.expr: a privileged component enumerates local programs and executes them to fingerprint them
the matching rule is a broad pattern over paths the unprivileged user can write

spec.method: read the regex/pattern used for service matching and test whether a world-writable directory satisfies it

preconditions.expr: the discovery runs with more privilege than the attacker (root, or through a root tunnel)

success: a binary the user created is executed by a root-owned process, evidenced by its side effect
the version string returned to the management plane comes from the attacker's file
no interaction from an administrator is needed — the discovery runs on its own schedule
failure_like: the enumerator only inspects known package metadata rather than executing discovered paths
it refuses binaries not owned by root or not in package-managed directories
false_positive: a user-installed tool appearing in an inventory listing — reporting is not executing
a crash from a malformed version output: the execution already happened, so treat it as the finding

hazards: any 'discover what is installed' agent has this shape: asset inventory, EDR telemetry, monitoring plugins, package auditors
the pattern is the vulnerability: a regex over paths is a whitelist the attacker can join by writing a file
the trigger is a schedule, not a request, so this can look non-reproducible in a lab — wait for the run
distinct from T-0047 (ordering inside a chroot) and T-0036 (argv re-read): here the privilege is fine and the *selection* is attacker-influenced
non_transfers: agents that resolve versions from package databases rather than by executing files
enumerators restricted to root-owned, package-managed directories

evidence.target: open-vm-tools service discovery / VMware Aria Operations SDMP (CVE-2025-41244)

provenance.author: NVISO research, CVE-2025-41244 (in-the-wild zero-day)
provenance.corroborates: the get_version function taking a regex pattern and a version command, the broad path match, and execution of non-system binaries as privileged

provenance.author: MITRE / NIST NVD
provenance.corroborates: CWE-267 privilege defined with unsafe actions; local privilege escalation
